items.followUp: Write the balanced equations for the reactions of chlorine with cold, dilute sodium hydroxide and hot, concentrated sodium hydroxide.

rubric.why: The cold-condition equation must show the products and be balanced.
rubric.description: Correct balanced reaction in cold conditions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the balanced equation producing sodium chloride and sodium hypochlorite.

rubric.why: The hot-condition equation must show the products and be balanced.
rubric.description: Correct balanced reaction in hot conditions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the balanced equation producing sodium chloride and sodium chlorate.

modelAnswer: Cold, dilute conditions: Cl₂ + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H₂O
Hot, concentrated conditions: 3Cl₂ + 6NaOH → 5NaCl + NaClO₃ + 3H₂O

items.followUp: State two physical properties of copper metal.

rubric.why: Silver's characteristic appearance is one of its properties.
rubric.description: Silver is a lustrous, shiny white metal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct description of its appearance.

rubric.why: A further characteristic metallic property is required.
rubric.description: Silver is an excellent conductor of heat and electricity; it is also malleable and ductile.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating a correct conductivity or mechanical property.

modelAnswer: Silver is a lustrous, shiny white metal.
It is an excellent conductor of heat and electricity, and is malleable and ductile.

items.followUp: Describe Rutherford's gold-foil experiment and state what it showed about the structure of the atom.

rubric.why: The experiment used alpha particles directed at a thin gold foil.
rubric.description: Rutherford directed alpha particles at a thin gold foil.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the alpha-particle beam and gold foil.

rubric.why: The scattered particles were detected by a screen around the foil.
rubric.description: A fluorescent screen was used to detect where particles went.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the screen used to detect the particles.

rubric.why: Most particles passed through without deflection.
rubric.description: Most alpha particles passed straight through the foil.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this observation.

rubric.why: A smaller number of particles changed direction, and a very few returned.
rubric.description: Some particles were deflected, while a very few bounced back.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the deflections or back-scattering.

rubric.why: These observations led to the nuclear model of the atom.
rubric.description: The atom is mostly empty space, with its positive charge and most of its mass concentrated in a tiny, dense nucleus at the centre.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the conclusion that a small central nucleus contains the positive charge and most of the mass.

modelAnswer: Rutherford directed a beam of alpha particles at a very thin gold foil.
A fluorescent screen around the foil detected the paths of the particles.
Most alpha particles passed straight through the foil without deflection.
Some particles were deflected, and a very few bounced back.
He concluded that most of the atom is empty space and that its positive charge and most of its mass are concentrated in a tiny, dense nucleus at the centre.

items.followUp: Give four examples of how chemistry is useful in agriculture, medicine, food, or clothing.

rubric.why: Chemistry contributes to agricultural products that improve crop growth or protect crops.
rubric.description: Chemistry helps agriculture through fertilizers and pesticides.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid agricultural application.

rubric.why: The manufacture of medicines is an important everyday application of chemistry.
rubric.description: Chemistry is used to prepare medicines and drugs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid medical application.

rubric.why: Chemistry helps prepare, process, or preserve food.
rubric.description: Chemistry is used in food processing and preservation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid food-related application.

rubric.why: Chemistry provides materials used to make clothing and other everyday goods.
rubric.description: Chemistry is used to make synthetic fibres such as nylon and polyester.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid clothing or materials application.

modelAnswer: Chemistry provides fertilizers and pesticides that help improve and protect crops.
It is used to prepare medicines and drugs to prevent and treat diseases.
It is used in food processing and in making food preservatives.
It is used to make synthetic fibres, such as nylon and polyester, for clothing.

items.followUp: Define a metallic bond and explain how it holds the particles in a metal together.

rubric.why: The definition must identify the electrostatic attraction responsible for metallic bonding.
rubric.description: A metallic bond is the electrostatic attraction between positive metal ions and delocalized electrons.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a clear definition identifying both the positive ions and delocalized electrons; award 1 mark if the attraction is named but one partner is missing.

rubric.why: The explanation should state what happens to the outer electrons in a metal.
rubric.description: Metal atoms release their outer electrons, which become delocalized and form a mobile sea of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the delocalized electron sea.

rubric.why: The explanation should connect the electron sea to the bonding of the metal ions.
rubric.description: The attraction between the electron sea and the positive ions holds the metal lattice together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining how this attraction holds the metal together.

modelAnswer: A metallic bond is the electrostatic attraction between positive metal ions and delocalized electrons.
Metal atoms release their outer electrons, which form a mobile sea of electrons around the positive ions.
The attraction between this electron sea and the positive ions holds the metal lattice together.

items.followUp: Define vapour pressure and explain why it increases when a liquid is heated.

rubric.why: A definition must identify vapour pressure as the pressure due to vapour above its liquid.
rubric.description: Vapour pressure is the pressure exerted by a vapour above its liquid in a closed container at a fixed temperature.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for identifying the pressure exerted by the vapour above its liquid; award 1 mark if the pressure is identified but the liquid/equilibrium context is unclear.

rubric.why: Vapour pressure is measured when evaporation and condensation have reached equilibrium in a closed system.
rubric.description: At equilibrium in a closed container, the vapour exerts this pressure over the liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the equilibrium or closed-container condition.

rubric.why: The effect of temperature is explained by increased particle kinetic energy.
rubric.description: When temperature rises, liquid particles gain kinetic energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking increased temperature with greater particle kinetic energy.

rubric.why: More particles escape into the vapour, increasing its pressure.
rubric.description: More particles enter the vapour, so the vapour pressure increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that vapour pressure rises as temperature rises.

modelAnswer: Vapour pressure is the pressure exerted by a vapour above its liquid in a closed container at a fixed temperature, when evaporation and condensation are in equilibrium.
As temperature increases, liquid particles gain kinetic energy and more of them escape into the vapour.
Therefore, the vapour pressure increases with an increase in temperature.

items.followUp: Define solubility and explain why sodium chloride dissolves in water.

rubric.why: Solubility describes the maximum amount of solute that forms a saturated solution in a specified amount of solvent.
rubric.description: Solubility is the maximum amount of a solute that dissolves in a given amount of solvent to form a saturated solution at a specified temperature.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the maximum amount, solvent, and saturated-solution idea; award 1 mark if the definition is substantially correct but incomplete.

rubric.why: The explanation should identify the ions that make up sodium chloride.
rubric.description: Sodium chloride consists of sodium and chloride ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying or showing the ions in NaCl.

rubric.why: Water's polar molecules attract and surround the ions, allowing NaCl to dissolve.
rubric.description: Polar water molecules attract and surround the sodium and chloride ions, so NaCl dissolves in water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining dissolution through attraction or hydration of the ions by water.

modelAnswer: Solubility is the maximum amount of a solute that dissolves in a given amount of solvent to form a saturated solution at a specified temperature.
Sodium chloride consists of Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions.
Water is polar; its molecules attract and surround these ions, allowing sodium chloride to dissolve.

items.followUp: Define a compound and give two examples.

rubric.why: An element is identified by the type of atoms it contains and its inability to be chemically decomposed into a simpler substance.
rubric.description: An element is a pure substance made of one kind of atom and cannot be decomposed into simpler substances by ordinary chemical methods.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Examples must be elements.
rubric.description: Examples include hydrogen and oxygen, or iron and copper.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for at least two correct examples.

modelAnswer: An element is a pure substance made of only one kind of atom and cannot be decomposed into simpler substances by ordinary chemical methods.
Examples: hydrogen and oxygen.
